text:
TCP Client Code Overview and Steps
1. Client Initialization and Connection
Code
: new 
TCPClient
(
hostname, username);
Description
: The 
TCPClient
 class initializes the client socket, sets up input/output streams, and begins threads to handle receiving and sending messages.
Tips
:
Make sure the server is running on the specified hostname and PORT.
Use try-catch blocks to handle potential 
IOException
 issues when connecting.
2. Receiving Server Messages (
ServerMessageHandler
)
Purpose
: This thread reads incoming messages from the server and prints them to the client console.
Code
:
java
while (running && (message = 
serverInput.readLine
()
) !
= null) {
    
System.out.println
(message
);
}
Tips
:
Always check if 
message !
= null to handle server disconnections gracefully.
Use running to control the thread lifecycle and ensure clean shutdowns.
The 
finally
 block in the run method closes connections if the client is disconnected.
3. Sending User Input (
UserInputHandler
)
Purpose
: This thread reads user input, sends it to the server, and allows the user to exit the session by typing /quit.
Code
:
java
serverOutput.writeBytes
(
userMessage
 + "\n"
);
serverOutput.flush
(
);
Tips
:
The flush method ensures messages are sent immediately to the server.
Use 
scanner.nextLine
() to capture entire lines of input.
Typing /quit triggers 
closeConnection
(
) to disconnect the client.
4. Connection Cleanup (
closeConnection
)
Purpose
: Close the socket connection and input/output streams when the client exits.
Code
:
java
if (
socket !
= null && !
socket.isClosed
()) {
    
socket.close
();
}
Tips
:
Always check if the socket is non-null and open before attempting to close it.
This method is also called in 
finally
 blocks to ensure cleanup occurs even if an exception is thrown.
TCP Server Code Overview and Steps
1. Server Initialization and Listening
Code
: 
ServerSocket
 
serverSocket
 = new 
ServerSocket
(
PORT);
Description
: The server listens 
on
 a specified PORT (12345) and handles multiple clients by creating a new thread (
ClientHandler
) for each connection.
Tips
:
The server uses a Shutdown Hook to handle interruptions (like 
Ctrl+C
) gracefully, setting running to false.
Use a 
ConcurrentHashMap
 to store active client connections safely across threads.
2. Accepting New Clients and Starting Threads
Purpose
: Each new client connection spawns a 
ClientHandler
 thread to manage communication.
Code
:
java
Socket 
clientSocket
 = 
serverSocket.accept
(
);
ClientHandler
 
clientHandler
 = new 
ClientHandler
(
clientSocket
, 
clientId
);
Tips
:
The server increments 
clientId
 for each connection to track clients.
The main loop terminates when running is set to false, closing all connections.
3. Handling Client Communication (
ClientHandler
)
Purpose
: Each 
ClientHandler
 handles messages from a single client and broadcasts messages to other clients.
Code
:
java
while ((message = 
input.readLine
()) != null && active) {
    
broadcast(
username + ": " + message + "\n");
}
Tips
:
The 
readLine
 method returns null when the client disconnects, allowing the loop to exit.
active indicates if the client is currently connected, and 
clientHandlers.put
(
username, this); adds the client to the active clients list.
4. Broadcasting Messages
Purpose
: The broadcast method sends messages to all other active clients.
Code
:
java
clientHandlers.forEach
((user, handler) -> {
    if (
handler !
= this) {
        
handler.output
.writeBytes
(message);
    }
});
Tips
:
Use 
clientHandlers.forEach
 to iterate over all active clients except the sender (this).
Handle 
IOException
 within the loop to avoid crashes if a client is disconnected.
5. Cleaning Up Connections (
closeConnection
)
Purpose
: Remove the client from 
clientHandlers
 and close its socket.
Code
:
java
clientHandlers.remove
(username
);
socket.close
();
Tips
:
Removing the client from 
clientHandlers
 ensures no further messages are sent to this client.
This method is called in finally blocks to guarantee cleanup if an exception occurs.
General Tips for Running and Testing
Testing
: Start the server first, then connect multiple clients using different usernames.
Error Handling
: Ensure the client handles server disconnections and vice versa, to avoid crashes during abrupt disconnections.
Resources
: Use try-with-resources or explicit 
close(
) calls for streams and sockets to prevent memory leaks.
Shutdown Management
: Use a Shutdown Hook in the server and handle /quit command on the client for smooth disconnections.
These steps and tips should provide a solid foundation for understanding and expanding on this basic client-server communication setup.
